CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for anxiety management and general health maintenance.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 45-year-old female (DOB 08/01/1980) presenting for follow-up. She reports that her anxiety has improved significantly since starting Buspar, which was recently prescribed by Dr. Brown. She notes that her anxiety was severe in November and December, with symptoms typically starting during the workday. She attributes this to multiple factors: recent initiation of Singulair by Dr. Ward (which can cause anxiety as a side effect), work-related stress from leading the process of delivering COVID test results to patients and opening evaluation centers and a COVID clinic, and feeling guilty about not being on the front lines during the pandemic. She notes that in November and December, her anxiety would spike the week before her menstrual period, then progressed to random spikes. She is currently feeling better. Regarding weight, she reports stopping Camila birth control due to excessive hunger while on it, and notes she has lost some weight over the past six months. She denies other health concerns.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies other current health issues. She reports continued itching/discomfort managed with cream, used once weekly with good effect. She requests refill of vaginal cream for the first time.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Anxiety (recent, November-December)
Breast lumps/fibroadenomas (previously evaluated, patient reports they feel smaller but still present)
Abnormal Pap smear approximately 2009, required surveillance every six months for a period, subsequently normalized
Irregular periods (previously managed with progesterone)
Vulvovaginal discomfort

MEDICATIONS
Buspar (recently started by Dr. Brown for anxiety)
Progesterone (for menstrual regulation)
Singulair (prescribed by Dr. Ward)
Vaginal cream (used once weekly for itching/discomfort)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at approximately age 45

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works in healthcare setting, involved in COVID testing/clinic operations. Married with two children. Received COVID vaccine; husband and daughter have not been vaccinated. Son has received first vaccine dose.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Neck: Small bumps palpated, no acute findings
Thyroid: Normal on palpation
Breasts: Left breast feels slightly denser; tender to palpation in lower left quadrant where patient previously had clogging during breastfeeding; lumps palpable bilaterally but reported by patient to be smaller than previously; right breast without acute findings
Abdomen: Deferred
Pelvic exam: Within normal limits

RESULTS
Pap smear from 2019: Negative/negative

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Anxiety: Well-controlled on Buspar. Continue current management. Anxiety likely multifactorial (work stress, potential Singulair side effect, hormonal factors, life stressors). Continue to monitor.
2. Breast lumps/fibroadenomas: Benign findings, likely related to hormonal/menstrual cycle changes. Continue monitoring. Patient expressing concern given family history of breast cancer (mother at age 45). Discussed that these are benign and haven't changed, which is reassuring. Patient to follow up with breast specialist; referral sent and patient will be contacted within couple of business days to schedule appointment. Breast specialist may perform in-office ultrasound and can perform procedures if needed.
3. Pap smear: Last normal Pap in 2019. Patient has history of abnormal Pap around 2009. Repeat Pap smear recommended today given patient's immunocompromised state, stress, and physician's observation of increased abnormal Paps in previously healthy patients; performed today.
4. Vaginal cream: Prescription refilled for ongoing use as needed.
5. General: Patient counseled regarding breast cancer risk and surveillance. Reassured that lack of changes in breast findings is reassuring for malignancy.
